natural_language_statement:
The definitions of the module `MIPRE.Foundations.Distances` of the MIP\* = RE formalization (commit `70cbf1c` of vidick/MIPRE-formalization). Distance measures. This file contains the definitions of the blueprint subsection "Distance measures" (Section 2, "Foundations"): the dimension-normalized Hilbert--Schmidt inner product and squared norm on complex matrices, and the distance between two families of POVMs relative to a question distribution.

definition_title: Definitions of Cnf: 3SAT and decoupled 5SAT formulas Literals, clauses and satisfaction, for the succinct Cook–Levin theorem…
natural_language_statement:
The definitions of the module `MIPRE.Foundations.SAT.Cnf` of the MIP\* = RE formalization (commit `70cbf1c` of vidick/MIPRE-formalization). 3SAT and decoupled 5SAT formulas. Literals, clauses and satisfaction, for the succinct Cook–Levin theorem (`planning/succinct-cook-levin.md`). A 3SAT formula is a *set* of clauses, each of exactly three literals (a clause of fewer literals repeats one: `x ∨ x ∨ x`), and a decoupled 5SAT formula (`answer_reduction.tex`, "Decoupled 5SAT and its succinct descriptions") is a set of clauses with one literal from each of five blocks of variables, evaluated on five separate assignments. The literal `x^o` of the paper is `⟨x, o⟩`: positive when `o = true`.

**Definitions** (10): `MIPRE.SAT.Clause3` (A 3SAT clause.); `MIPRE.SAT.Clause3.eval` (The value of a clause.); `MIPRE.SAT.Clause5` (A decoupled 5SAT clause: one literal from each of five blocks.); `MIPRE.SAT.Clause5.eval` (The value of a decoupled clause on five assignments.); `MIPRE.SAT.Cnf3` (A 3SAT formula on the variables `V`: a set of clauses.); `MIPRE.SAT.Cnf3.Sat` (`w` satisfies every clause of `φ`.); `MIPRE.SAT.Cnf5` (A decoupled 5SAT formula.); `MIPRE.SAT.Cnf5.Sat` (The five assignments satisfy every clause of `φ`.); `MIPRE.SAT.Lit` (A literal: a variable and its sign (`pos = true` for `x`, `false` for `¬x`).); `MIPRE.SAT.Lit.eval` (The value of a literal under an assignment.).

natural_language_statement:
The definitions of the module `MIPRE.Foundations.LowDegree.BinaryPower` of the MIP\* = RE formalization (commit `70cbf1c` of vidick/MIPRE-formalization). The definitions of the module `MIPRE.TM.Interp.Machine` of the MIP\* = RE formalization (commit `70cbf1c` of vidick/MIPRE-formalization). The interpreter machine. `U` is the multi-input Turing machine interpreting the programs of `Instr.lean`: a state is a program, a position in it and the phase of the instruction there (`Ctl`), and one step executes one phase of the current instruction (`execInstr`), producing head moves, writes, an optional output symbol and the next control: the same instruction in another phase, the next instruction, a jump to the start of another program, or a halt. natural_language_statement:
The definitions of the module `MIPRE.TM.Interp.CopyTree` of the MIP\* = RE formalization (commit `70cbf1c` of vidick/MIPRE-formalization). The `copyTree` routine. Copying (or skipping) a preorder-serialized value: a scan with a unary counter of the pending subtrees on `CNT`, one more per `1` (a node with two children, itself consumed) and one fewer per `0` (a leaf), finishing when none is pending. The scan from `d ≥ 1` pending subtrees over `S(v)` leaves `d - 1` pending (`copyTree_scan`), finishing when `d = 1`; the instruction starts with one (`exec_copyTree`).

definition_title: Definitions of GetEnv: The `getEnv` routine With the unary index `S(ofNat i)` under the head of `C` and the environment `envRepr env` on `E`…
natural_language_statement:
The definitions of the module `MIPRE.TM.Interp.GetEnv` of the MIP\* = RE formalization (commit `70cbf1c` of vidick/MIPRE-formalization). The `getEnv` routine. With the unary index `S(ofNat i)` under the head of `C` and the environment `envRepr env` on `E` with its head at the end, `getEnv` writes `S(env.get i)` at the head of `X`: it walks left over `i` separators (phases `p1`–`p3`), then to the start of the element (`p4`), copies it (`p5`) and returns the head of `E` to the end (`p8`); past the start of the environment the index is out of range, the rest of it is consumed (`p6`, `p7`) and `nil` is written (`p9`). The proof is by induction on the index, over the suffix of the environment not yet passed.

**Definitions** (1): `MIPRE.TM.Interp.EnvTape` (A tape holding the environment from `0`, blank before.).

definition_title: Definitions of Table: Every Boolean function has a circuit The formula of a Boolean function on `N` bits from its truth table (`Fml.table`):…
natural_language_statement:
The definitions of the module `MIPRE.Foundations.SAT.Table` of the MIP\* = RE formalization (commit `70cbf1c` of vidick/MIPRE-formalization). Every Boolean function has a circuit. The formula of a Boolean function on `N` bits from its truth table (`Fml.table`): a mux tree on the bits, of size at most `7 · 2^N`. Its circuit is well-formed (`Fml.toCircuit_wellFormed`) and computes the function (`Fml.eval_table`). This is how the check circuit of the Cook–Levin tableau of the interpreter machine is obtained: from the truth table of the local check predicate, as in the paper's `lem:pack-check-size` (`planning/succinct-cook-levin.md`, S3).

**Definitions** (1): `MIPRE.SAT.Fml.table` (The formula of a Boolean function on `N` bits: a mux tree on the bits, the leaves being the entries of the truth table.).

definition_title: Definitions of AnsEnd: The answer tapes end at `T` Two clauses beyond the tableau: the cell at position `T + 3` of each of the two free tapes…
natural_language_statement:
The definitions of the module `MIPRE.TM.CookLevin.AnsEnd` of the MIP\* = RE formalization (commit `70cbf1c` of vidick/MIPRE-formalization). The answer tapes end at `T`. Two clauses beyond the tableau: the cell at position `T + 3` of each of the two free tapes holds the blank. They are what makes the soundness direction of the describer give answers of length at most `T`: the free-tape clauses force the blanks of a free tape to be trailing (`freeClauses`), so a blank at `T + 3` bounds the string read off the time-`0` row by `T` (`freeLen`, `Sound.lean`). An accepting run on answers of length at most `T` satisfies them, so they cost the completeness direction nothing. `tableauPlus` is the tableau together with them, `tableauPlusF`…

natural_language_statement:
The definitions of the module `MIPRE.TM.CookLevin.LayoutProg` of the MIP\* = RE formalization (commit `70cbf1c` of vidick/MIPRE-formalization). The layout arithmetic as programs. The widths and offsets of the index layout (`Layout.lean`) as programs. Two conventions make them cheap: * **widths and offsets are unary.** `W e`, `mOf e G`, the field offsets: all are affine in `e` with small coefficients, so in unary they are `append` and iterated `append`, and no arithmetic program is needed. `e` itself must be unary in any case — the formulas are of size polynomial in `e`, so a binary `e` would make the output exponential in the input. * **a constant of a field is a resize of a bit string.** `resize w bs` keeps the low `w` bits of `bs`,…

definition_title: Definitions of DecoupledProg: The decoupled describer as a program, and `ℓ₀` `ℓ₀ = ⌈log 2T⌉` is pinned by its specification, `2T ≤ 2^{ℓ₀} < 4T` for…
natural_language_statement:
The definitions of the module `MIPRE.TM.CookLevin.DecoupledProg` of the MIP\* = RE formalization (commit `70cbf1c` of vidick/MIPRE-formalization). The decoupled describer as a program, and `ℓ₀`. `ℓ₀ = ⌈log 2T⌉` is pinned by its specification, `2T ≤ 2^{ℓ₀} < 4T` for `T ≥ 1`, so it cannot be replaced by the cheaper `Nat.size T + 1`, which is right except at powers of two, where it gives `4T` and violates the strict bound.
